# SealSecurity — Pre-Commit Secrets Guard for Agentic Code

> *"AI agents commit hardcoded keys at machine speed. Traditional code review can't catch them."* — Cycode 2026 Threat Analysis

**SealSecurity** prevents hardcoded secrets — API keys, tokens, passwords, certificates, and cloud credentials — from reaching your repository, with special attention to patterns commonly generated by AI coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, GPT).

## The Problem

- Check Point Research confirmed autonomous AI agents breached 9 government agencies using tools like Claude Code
- 45% of AI-generated code contains security vulnerabilities at 2.74x the density of human code
- AI agents frequently write IaC templates with hardcoded keys and over-permissioned IAM roles
- Traditional pre-commit hooks lack agent-specific pattern detection

## Features

- **Agent Pattern Detection** — Identifies credential injection patterns unique to AI code generation (inline env vars, hardcoded SDK init, embedded connection strings)
- **Push Protection** — Blocks `git push` if secrets are detected, even if they bypassed pre-commit
- **Cloud Provider Signatures** — Scans for AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI/DO credentials in any file type
- **IaC-Aware** — Detects hardcoded secrets in Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi, Helm charts
- **False Positive Tuning** — Allows developer annotations (`seal-skip-line`) for legitimate test credentials
- **GitHub Action Mode** — Runs as a CI gate on pull requests
- **Extensible** — Add custom regex patterns via `.sealpatterns.json`

## Quick Start

### Install

```bash
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOUR_ORG/seal-security/main/install.sh | bash
```

Or clone and run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_ORG/ai-security-toolkit
cd ai-security-toolkit/seal-security
bash install.sh
```

### Configure

```bash
# Basic configuration (run from repo root)
seal-security init

# Set strict mode (blocks push)
seal-security config set block-push true

# Add custom patterns
seal-security patterns add "AI_API_KEY=[A-Za-z0-9]{32,48}"
```

### Run Manually

```bash
seal-security scan --path . --format json --output report.json
```

## GitHub Action Integration

```yaml
# .github/workflows/seal-security.yml
name: SealSecurity
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run SealSecurity
        uses: ./seal-security/action
        with:
          block-push: true
          report-format: sarif
          upload-artifact: true
```

## Pre-Commit Hook (Manual)

In `.git/hooks/pre-commit`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "🔒 SealSecurity — scanning for hardcoded secrets..."
RESULTS=$(python3 "$(dirname "$0")/../seal-security/seal.py" scan --path . --format json)
if echo "$RESULTS" | python3 -c "import sys,json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); exit(0 if len(data['secrets'])==0 else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "✅ No secrets found"
    exit 0
else
    echo "❌ Secrets detected! Commit blocked. Run 'seal-security scan --path .' for details."
    exit 1
fi
```

## CHECKLIST.md — Monthly Review

- [ ] Update `patterns/agent.json` with new AI agent credential patterns
- [ ] Review false positives from the last 30 days
- [ ] Check for new cloud provider credential formats
- [ ] Verify pre-commit hook is installed on all developer machines
- [ ] Run seal-security across the entire repository history
- [ ] Audit bypassed commits (secrets caught after push but before merge)

## Maintenance

This tool is a **living defense**. AI agents evolve rapidly — new tools emerge with new coding patterns. Revisit this repo every 30 days and check for updated patterns.
